title: Geothermal for apartment buildings: performance, silence and shared savings
excerpt: The energy transition of apartment buildings is a major challenge in Belgium. With ever stricter EPC standards and soaring fossil fuel prices, co-owned buildings are looking for sustainable alternatives.
author: WellDoneDrill

children.text: The energy transition of apartment buildings is a major challenge in Belgium. Between ever stricter EPC (PEB) standards and soaring fossil fuel prices, co-owned buildings are looking for sustainable alternatives. At
WellDoneDrill
, we install vertical drilling systems capable of heating and cooling entire buildings. Here is why geothermal is the most relevant solution for multi-unit housing.
1. No more noise and visual clutter

This is the number one problem with air-to-water heat pumps in dense urban areas: noise. Installing dozens of outdoor units on balconies or the roof creates unbearable noise for the neighbours and spoils the building's façade.
Complete discretion:
With geothermal, everything happens underground and in the basement. There is no outdoor fan, no vibration and nothing visible from the street.
Respecting planning rules:
In Brussels or historic town centres in Wallonia, planning regulations often ban air-conditioning units on façades. Geothermal elegantly avoids this constraint.
2. Geocooling: summer comfort without higher service charges
Global warming makes apartments (especially top-floor ones) stifling in summer. Installing conventional air conditioning in every unit sends shared electricity costs through the roof.
Passive cooling:
The network of probes at 150 metres circulates 12 °C water through the apartments' underfloor heating.
Economies of scale:
This cooling is almost free (only the circulator uses a little energy). It is a strong selling point for landlords and unrivalled comfort for residents.
3. Sharing the borehole field to cut costs
A big advantage of co-ownership is
pooling the investment
. Instead of each owner installing their own system, a shared geothermal borehole field is created.
Optimised space:
Several 150-metre boreholes (a borehole field) are drilled under the car park or the shared garden of the residence.
Tailored output:
The geothermal plant in the basement distributes heat according to the actual needs of each apartment, optimising the building's overall efficiency.
4. An immediate boost to property value
A building heated by geothermal energy benefits from an
outstanding EPC rating
On resale:
An apartment rated A or B sells faster and for more than one heated by gas or oil.
Energy independence:
The co-ownership is freed from fuel deliveries and geopolitical swings in gas prices. The "fuel" (the Earth's heat) belongs to the co-ownership.
5. An installation that (literally) lasts a lifetime
While a communal boiler must be replaced every 15 years, the borehole field built by
WellDoneDrill

is guaranteed for more than 50 years. It is a structural investment in the building. Only the heat pump in the plant room will need servicing or replacement in the long run; the ground loop infrastructure stays in the ground for generations.
Conclusion

For a co-owned building, geothermal is not an expense but a strategy to protect the building's value. It offers premium comfort (heating and cooling), ends neighbour disputes over noise and cuts energy bills by a factor of four. At WellDoneDrill, we support property managers and owners' associations from the feasibility study to commissioning.

seoDescription: Why geothermal suits co-owned buildings: no noise, free cooling, a shared borehole field, a better EPC rating and an installation built for 50 years.
